findings.problem: Earlier operands and function arguments remain variable locations instead of captured values when later calls mutate globals; augmented assignment has the same problem.
findings.example: g = 7; g + change() where change sets g=12 and returns 3
findings.proposal: A shared value-snapshot/liveness contract for arithmetic, comparisons, calls, assignments, and future tuple lowering; differential side-effect regressions.

findings.area: direct BoolOp and both chained-comparison paths
findings.problem: Direct and/or evaluates all operands. Both frontends evaluate every chained-comparison operand before testing earlier comparisons.
findings.example: if 0 and touch(): pass; if 2 < 1 < touch(): pass
findings.observed: direct invokes touch for both; c invokes touch for the chained comparison
findings.classification: Direct non-short-circuit behavior is also a documented v0 limitation; the existing claim of identical backend semantics is too broad.
findings.proposal: Lazy branch lowering with operands evaluated only when reached; preserve Python and/or operand-return semantics or explicitly distinguish the documented boolean-normalization contract.

findings.problem: Range bounds are not always frozen before binding the loop target; changing a bound or assigning to the target changes iteration. Loop exit exposes the incremented target rather than Python's final target value.
examples: limit=3; for i in range(limit): ...; limit=0
i=99; for i in range(3): pass; putchar(48+i)
findings.proposal: Capture range arguments before target binding; keep a hidden iterator independent of the visible loop variable; guard overflow and descending-range termination.

findings.problem: The destination is zeroed as a boolean flag before its old value is read in the comparison.
findings.proposal: Evaluate the complete RHS into a fresh value before storing to the assignment destination.

findings.problem: Default-fill seeds are read from mutable source cells when first materialized. Shared derived caches then contaminate copies and reset snapshots. Looking at memory before a step can change later observed memory. Reinitialization also leaves old explicit cells behind.
findings.proposal: Freeze initialization seeds independently of mutations; share only caches derived from immutable initialization; clear overlays on reinitialization. Integrate with, but do not postpone correctness behind, compact memory storage.

findings.problem: C accepts self-initialization and possibly-unbound names after conditionals/empty loops; direct rejects them. Direct also rejects proven constant-true binding. Both accept a global declaration after prior use that CPython rejects.
findings.proposal: Separate declarations from assigned-value state, merge branch/loop binding states, and use a Python compile-time syntax validation pass; unify the accepted-subset contract.

findings.problem: An output path may overwrite the Python input; failed output writes leak tracebacks, and output is written directly rather than replaced atomically.
findings.proposal: Preflight same-file/output collisions and parent paths; write a temporary file then atomically replace; format file/encoding errors without raw traceback.

findings.problem: Large compiled input uses a Python list and per-address dict, and debugger initialization copies the dict. The final Fibonacci artifact could not finish under the bounded 4GiB Python CLI benchmark.
findings.proposal: Compact source parsing plus typed mutable blocks or byte backing with a wide-word fallback, immutable fill seeds, and copy-on-write snapshots. A naive per-cell write dict can grow again because executed instructions self-modify.

findings.problem: Passing pure-value unit tests do not expose side-effect and iterator errors. Some e2e helpers check only stdout. Tuple-unpacking errors may point to a later use rather than the unsupported assignment.
findings.proposal: CPython/c/direct differential cases with side effects and cache-access order; check exit/stderr/stop reason; deterministic hash-seed canaries and original-source diagnostics.
findings.positive_observation: Both backends produced stable MC hashes under four PYTHONHASHSEED values in the spot check.

items: descending range and simple keyword arguments
consistent missing-return/None, runtime zero division, unsigned/signed and EOF contracts
findings.proposal: Add inexpensive AST lowering after the core value/iteration contracts are fixed, rather than requiring source-level helpers or silently accepting incorrect semantics.

findings.problem: Small constant multiplies still inject a generic helper; its bit powers are recomputed in nested loops. The compiler retains full intermediate strings. Debug history evicts via list.pop(0).
findings.proposal: Constant strength reduction and helper specialization, cached/streamed stages, circular history and output deltas; measure end-to-end before claiming speedups.

history_microbenchmark.scope: Isolated history-container maintenance, not a debugger speedup measurement.

limits: Known layout-dependent compiler counterexamples were inspected but their gated slow reproductions were not rerun; their status after recent code-generation changes needs separate validation.

The original-Malbolge examples suite, Python-frontend large e2e suites, web/UI journeys, and every resource/termination edge case were not exhaustively verified. Assembler and compiled-fixture conformance received an additional 17 passing tests.
The new correctness counterexamples do not invalidate the previously measured Fibonacci inputs, which have separate validated artifacts.
